decisions.accepted_scope: Develop distinct ordinary pitches with clear tactical purposes, readable behavior and weaknesses. PH-02-R1 fixes exactly three ordinary pitches per pitcher, with character-specific selections from a shared library; charging modifies a pitch and Star Pitches sit outside the count. PH-02-R2 fixes the library as fastball, changeup, curveball, slider and sinker with their recorded game roles. PH-15-R1/R2/R4 fix universal fastball access and starting assignments for all 25 existing characters. PH-02-R3 requires ordinary pitch selection before charge, with the type locked at charge start and a common charge/release action. PH-02-R4 selects one button cycling through the three ordinary pitches before charge. PH-02-R5 sets RB/Tab cycling in accepted repertoire order, resets each new pitch to Fastball, retains common charge/release and displays the available pitch order without identifying the active selection. Detailed presentation, input/state edge handling, weaknesses/counterplay and numerical tuning remain open; location and live steering follow PH-03/PH-04. This is direction acceptance, not implementation or human playtest acceptance. Original scopes are preserved in history and each refinement.

validation_evidence.summary: P1-c adds the pure sim selection step beside ChargeButton: PitchSelectionState(Slot, Locked) with slot 0 = fastball as the default, and PitchSelection.Advance applying one SET tick in order - a cycle press while unlocked and selectable advances to the next selectable slot and wraps, the tick the charge arms locks the slot as it stands after that cycle (so a press on the arming tick is never dropped, including the same-tick press-and-release), the commit throws the locked family and resets to fastball unlocked, and a disarm with no delivery releases the lock and keeps the slot. A family with no authored row in the active table is skipped, so no press can select a pitch that cannot fly; a stale slot reads as the fastball; a table with no fastball row stops by name. Match.SelectPitch / Match.FamilyAt read the current Pitcher.Repertoire and the match's own pitching.families, never Rules.Default. Scenarios S-101 (all 25 repertoires under a table that authors all five), S-102 (later presses ignored, quick and MAX releases), S-103 (cycle then lock on one tick), S-104 (reset at every SET entry and after a swap, on a real match through a delivery, a foul and a dead pickoff), S-105 (the shipped root skips curveball, slider and sinker), S-106 (the disarm edge and a closed seat), plus determinism and the defensive read; every row drives the real ChargeButton and holds on both data roots. Nothing in the running game calls the step yet, so no behaviour moved: cli match --seed 7 is byte-identical and the #708 evidence regenerated with source-hash changes only. Review hardening in the same PR: the lock is held by an invariant rather than only by the releasing edge - a locked state whose charge button is not armed is stale and is read as unlocked, so a SET frame that returns early (the swap pick, a pause, a tutorial gate) and skips the tick the charge went away cannot strand the selection locked with every cycle press ignored until the next reset. S-106b drives that through the real ChargeButton and pins that a genuinely armed charge still ignores presses.

validation_evidence.summary: P1-g puts the CPU pitcher behind one switch, pitching.cpu.humanInputs: false on the shipped root and true in trials/pitch5 (PH-18-R1 - the CPU converts in the same trial as the new shapes, no interim flat CPU). Off, Match.CpuPitch runs the shipped endpoint model unchanged - same body, same draws, same order - and cli match --seed 7 on the shipped root is byte-identical before and after, as is the S-29 cohort. On, Match.CpuPitchByInputs builds the delivery from the inputs a hand has and nothing else: the count row's location is a horizontal intent in feet and the body walks the rubber until the family's own crossing lands on it (the crossing is affine in the rubber, so the solve is (intent - X0) / HomeSet.PitcherWalk with X0 the same delivery from the middle, clamped to the legal +/-1); AimX and AimY are always 0 and the height is the family's dropFt; the family is the row's per-family weights filtered to the slots PitchSelection.IsSelectable allows and then expressed as the 0/1/2 cycle presses it is; charge and steer are two independent modifier rolls rather than exclusive verbs, so a charged CPU pitch is still steerable; and the stick is PitchFlight.BreakReach over this delivery's own air time rather than an instant +/-1. The arm is stamped before the solve, which P1-d found was not the case - the same delivery from the wrong arm misses its intent by exactly twice the family's sweep. Scatter moved onto the rubber intent in X, because there is no vertical input to miss in; TIRED still widens it, and PreparePitch's TIRED wobble is unchanged and is not a CPU privilege. The shipped file authors the new fields inert, holding the port of today's exclusive mix written down (fastball = normal + charge + break, chargeChance = charge / total, steerChance = break / total). The CPU now walks that same cycle: its choice is replayed through PitchSelection.Advance from PitchSelectionState.Reset and is always 0, 1 or 2 presses.

validation_evidence.finding: Finding for sitting 1, reported and not fixed: the CPU's rubber walk cannot always finish before the pitcher-ready beat. The walk runs at the hand's own rate, 1.6 rubber units per second, and feel.pitcherReadySeconds is 0.55, so at most 0.88 of a rubber unit (2.11 ft) is covered before the delivery; a larger move - and under the trial the rubber is the location on every pitch, so a two-unit traverse is reachable - finishes with the body snapping the remainder at the launch, where it is put on the delivery's own rubber so the arm and the ball agree. No number was changed to hide this.

decisions.accepted_scope: Keep stars supplementary to the ordinary pitching/hitting duel. PH-16-R14 selects no plate-level chemistry bonus; existing fielding/teamwork chemistry remains unchanged. Ordinary play must remain satisfying and complete on its own; specials create occasional tactical opportunities with readable counterplay rather than becoming the central at-bat resource strategy. Specials do not guarantee hits or outs. PH-16-R1 keeps the ordinary timing window for Star Pitches, whose challenge comes from readable ball behavior. Existing timing-reducing Star Pitches require separately reviewed replacement effects and reconciliation before implementation. PH-16-R2 permits ability-specific Star Swing contact-area changes, including extra spatial forgiveness, while requiring actual geometric contact. Eligible abilities, regions and Contact/charge interactions remain separately reviewed; this is not a universal bonus. PH-16-R3 requires a missed Star Swing to spend its full normal resource cost, without a miss discount/refund. PH-16-R4 gives each team one shared resource pool for Star Pitches and Star Swings, independent of the opposing team. PH-16-R5 grants both teams modest gains after completed plate appearances plus bonuses for successful plays. PH-16-R6 gives both teams a usable starting reserve so a special is available from the opening plate appearance. PH-16-R7 accepts a small set of ability cost tiers. PH-16-R8 resolves captain eligibility: the highest-cost specials are captain-exclusive, while role players use lower-cost specials; individual assignments remain open. PH-16-R9 gives each character one Star Pitch and one Star Swing, separate from ordinary pitches, with no selection among multiple specials. PH-16-R10 activates specials with a held modifier plus the normal pitch/swing action, preserving the charge/release rhythm. PH-16-R11 samples and locks special intent at accepted action-button release, allowing changes while charging but none afterward; ordinary family locking remains at charge start. PH-16-R12 falls back to the ordinary action at intended timing when Stars are insufficient, spending no Stars and showing clear unavailable feedback; a red flash at the Star counter remains a presentation candidate. PH-16-R13 applies ordinary charge tradeoffs alongside special effects, retaining ability-specific contact-area changes; exact composition remains open. Exact activation bindings, resource lifecycle, charge formulas/interactions, tier count, prices/assignments, capacity, starting amount, reset rules, base gains, bonus events/amounts, stacking rules, ability prices, deduction timing, cancellation/foul policy, replacement effects and frequency remain open. Existing gameplay-spec D6 and other special-ability restrictions remain in force. Direction acceptance only; no runtime change or human playtest acceptance.
